context.requirement_text:
Second half of ISS-0431/GH#835's fix for its own stated PRIMARY
surface, atop REQ-216's core module. Mirrors REQ-186/REQ-187's and
REQ-214/REQ-215's own "core module first, wiring requirement(s)
second, disjoint files" split precedent in this file.

TWO ADMISSION GATES, NOT ONE, because tenant identity is not known
until partway through `Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline`'s existing chain --
read in full (lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex): `Plug.Parsers` runs
first, then `assign_trace_id`, then `Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline`
(which itself resolves tenant identity via a DB read -- token
verification, tenant-by-realm/slug resolution, JIT provisioning --
i.e. AuthPipeline's OWN work already consumes a DB connection BEFORE
any tenant identity exists to gate on), then
`Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`, then `match`/`dispatch`. Given that
ordering, a single per-tenant-only gate cannot run early enough to
cover AuthPipeline's own connection use. Resolved as follows, stated
as an accepted, disclosed limitation rather than silently glossed
over (matching this project's own honesty convention for a limitation
that cannot be fully closed within one requirement's scope, e.g.
decision 0014's own disclosed WASM native-crash gap):

1. GLOBAL gate, mounted FIRST in the chain -- before `Plug.Parsers`,
so a request rejected for lack of capacity is rejected before any
body-parsing work is spent on it. Calls
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire(:global)`. Covers AuthPipeline's own
connection use (the gap named above) because it runs before
AuthPipeline and gates ALL downstream DB-connection-holding work,
auth included.
2. PER-TENANT gate, mounted immediately AFTER `Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline`
(tenant identity now resolved into `conn.assigns.auth_context.tenant_id`)
and BEFORE `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`/`match`/`dispatch`. Calls
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire({:tenant, schema_name})`, resolving
`schema_name` the same way `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus` and
`Letflow.Scheduler.Poller` already do (tenant-id -> schema-name
resolution already exists in this codebase; reuse it, do not
re-derive). Covers TenantStatus's own DB lookup and every sub-router's
dispatch work -- the dominant share of connection-holding time per
REQ-056/ISS-0431's own round-trip profiling.
DISCLOSED LIMITATION: AuthPipeline's own DB work (steps 1-4 of its
moduledoc) is covered by the global gate only, not a per-tenant one,
because tenant identity does not exist yet at that point in the
chain. This is accepted, not silently omitted -- state it in this
plug's own moduledoc.
3. Both gates: on `{:error, :capacity}`, respond immediately (halt the
plug chain, no further plugs run) via
`Letflow.Api.Response.service_unavailable/2` (REQ-066, ALREADY
EXISTING -- do not add a new response helper), with the
`Retry-After` header set explicitly on the conn first (matching
`Response.rate_limited/2`'s own documented "caller sets Retry-After"
convention) to a fixed, configured seconds value (config, default 1)
-- NOT a computed estimate, since this admission mechanism has no
queueing/backoff-timing model to estimate from (a fixed short value
matching `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`'s own existing `@retry_after_seconds
"30"` precedent's SHAPE, though the specific number here is
independently justified: admission rejection is a near-instant
decision with no wait queue behind it, unlike TenantStatus's
migration-in-progress case, so a MUCH shorter retry-after is
appropriate -- state this reasoning in the plug's moduledoc rather
than copying TenantStatus's 30-second value uncritically).
4. On success at BOTH gates: the plug stores both `admission_ref()`s
in `conn.assigns` and registers a `Plug.Conn.register_before_send/2`
(or equivalent, matching how this codebase already threads
request-scoped cleanup -- state which mechanism is chosen and why) or
calls `Letflow.Admission.release/1` for both refs when the response is
sent, so an admitted request's slot is freed exactly once, on every
response path including a request that raises inside a downstream
plug or router (verified in the acceptance criteria below).
NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no change to REQ-216's core semaphore logic;
no change to `Letflow.Plugs.RateLimit` (still deferred, unmounted,
unrelated mechanism); no Poller wiring (REQ-218); no tier-weighted
per-tenant caps (REQ-216's own recorded open question).

task.description: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (WF-02 Step 1b) hard gate on lib/letflow/design/req217-http-admission-wiring.md before it is eligible for ELIXIR-DEV.
acceptance_criteria: with REQ-216's global cap artificially forced to 0 (test config override), every request to any /api/v1/* route -- including one that would otherwise pass auth -- receives HTTP 503 with a Retry-After header and Plug.Parsers never runs (no body-parsing side effect observable), confirmed by a request carrying a body too large for the parser's own limit still returning 503 rather than 413

with the global cap open but a specific tenant's per-tenant cap artificially forced to 0, a request authenticated as that tenant receives HTTP 503 with Retry-After, while a request authenticated as a DIFFERENT tenant (same global cap) succeeds -- both requests observed in the same test

a successfully admitted request that completes normally releases both its global and per-tenant admission_ref()s exactly once, verified by exhausting the cap, making one full round-trip request, and observing a subsequent request now succeeds

a successfully admitted request whose downstream handler RAISES still releases both admission_ref()s (no permanent slot leak on an error path) -- a test that forces a raise in a route handler and then verifies a subsequent request still succeeds

the 503 response body matches Letflow.Api.Response.service_unavailable/2's existing Error.service_unavailable/1 document shape exactly (same fields REQ-066's own test/letflow/api/error_test.exs already asserts), confirmed by comparing against that existing test's expected shape rather than asserting a new ad hoc body shape

the plug chain order change is confirmed by reading lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex: the global admission plug is the very first plug (before Plug.Parsers), and the per-tenant admission plug is positioned after Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline and before Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted

checks_performed.crash_safety_independent_verification: Read deps/bandit/lib/bandit/pipeline.ex and deps/plug/lib/plug/error_handler.ex directly, as instructed, plus deps/plug/lib/plug/router.ex and deps/plug/lib/plug/conn/wrapper_error.ex (NOT cited by the design's own §0 input list -- this omission is itself part of the finding). Confirmed CORRECT: (a) register_before_send/2 callbacks only fire inside Bandit.Pipeline.commit_response!/1, reached only on the non-exceptional path; Bandit's catch/rescue in run/5 jumps straight to handle_error/7 and commit_response!/1 never runs, so before_send is genuinely skipped on any raise that reaches Bandit's own boundary. Confirmed INCORRECT: the design's claim (design doc lines 104-109) that 'nothing here wraps the exception in a Plug.Conn.WrapperError... which nothing in this codebase does' is FALSE. Plug.Router's own generated dispatch/2 (deps/plug/lib/plug/router.ex:254-271) wraps any :error-kind exception raised by the matched route handler in Plug.Conn.WrapperError.reraise(conn, kind, reason, __STACKTRACE__) -- and the `conn` captured there is dispatch/2's own function parameter, i.e. the FULLY DOWNSTREAM conn (after both Admission mounts, AuthPipeline, and TenantStatus), which DOES carry the admission-ref assigns. This WrapperError then propagates to Plug.ErrorHandler's generated call/2 (deps/plug/lib/plug/error_handler.ex:78-96), which has a `rescue e in Plug.Conn.WrapperError` clause the design's trace never examined -- it only analyzed the `catch kind, reason ->` clause. That rescue clause extracts `conn = e.conn` (the DOWNSTREAM, assign-carrying conn) and passes THAT conn into handle_errors/2, not the pre-pipeline conn. So for AC4's literal scenario ('downstream handler RAISES'), conn.assigns in handle_errors/2 DOES reliably carry the admission refs via this WrapperError path -- the design's stated reason for needing the process-dictionary mechanism is factually wrong for exactly the case AC4 tests. The process-dictionary mechanism (Mechanism B) is still independently justifiable for a DIFFERENT, real gap the design never analyzes: a raise inside a PLUG that runs before dispatch (e.g. TenantStatus, AuthPipeline, or the tenant-derivation 'unreachable' crash branches inside Letflow.Plugs.Admission itself, per the design's own §2/OQ-2) is NOT wrapped in WrapperError (Plug.Builder's compiled pipeline has no per-plug try/catch of its own), so that raise DOES surface at Plug.ErrorHandler's `catch` clause with the pre-pipeline conn, exactly as the design describes -- but the design never distinguishes this case from the dispatch-stage case it got wrong, and never states which specific raise sites the process-dictionary mechanism is actually saving.
checks_performed.process_dictionary_precedent_check: Grepped lib/ for Process.put/Process.get/Plug.ErrorHandler usage. The design's OQ-1 claims 'no other Process.put/2 call site in lib/letflow/ as of this design' -- this is also FALSE. lib/letflow/engine/wasm/host_api.ex (lines 395-407, 587) and lib/letflow/engine/lua/platform.ex (lines 426, 752-753) already use Process.put/Process.get for exactly this class of problem (request/execution-scoped state that must survive across callback boundaries), under a documented `@staged_writes_pdict_key` / `@fail_signal_pdict_key` module-attribute naming convention. The design invented a bare, undocumented atom (`:letflow_admission_refs`) instead of following this codebase's own established pdict-key convention, and incorrectly raised the absence of precedent as an open question for REVIEWER rather than finding and following it.
checks_performed.single_plug_two_mount_ambiguity: Section 2's branch-behavior specification for pool: :tenant is otherwise complete (schema derivation success path, and the two 'should be unreachable' failure branches both explicitly resolved to 'crash, do not add a defensive Response.internal_error/1' with a stated rationale mirroring TenantStatus's own fail-closed precedent) -- this resolution is acceptable and does not itself require rework; flagging that OQ-2 is resolved by this review as 'crash is fine, no defensive response needed' so CODE-DESIGNER does not need to re-litigate it in the rework pass, only carry the decision through explicitly (moduledoc already commits to stating it per §8).
checks_performed.retry_after_justification: Adequate. §0 and §4 give a specific, non-copied rationale (try_acquire/2 is a synchronous GenServer.call over in-memory counters with no wait queue, so a slot frees on the timescale of another in-flight request's release/2 call -- expected sub-second -- versus TenantStatus's genuinely-can-take-tens-of-seconds migration wait). This check passes.
checks_performed.response_body_shape: Adequate. §3/§0 confirm the design routes exclusively through the existing Response.service_unavailable/2 -> Error.service_unavailable/1 path with no new body-shape invention, cross-referenced against test/letflow/api/error_test.exs's existing assertions. This check passes.
checks_performed.no_implementation_code: FAILED. Despite this exact repo having required two prior rework cycles on a DIFFERENT requirement (REQ-157, commits 3680243/290c6b2) specifically for literal Elixir code leaking into a 'design-only' doc, this design doc repeats the same anti-pattern extensively. Section 3 contains a literal executable pipe expression (`conn |> Plug.Conn.put_resp_header(...) |> Letflow.Api.Response.service_unavailable(...) |> Plug.Conn.halt()`), not a signature or type shape. Section 5 contains multiple literal, runnable code bodies: `Plug.Conn.assign(conn, assigns_key(pool), ref)`; a full `Plug.Conn.register_before_send(conn, fn conn -> release_if_present(conn, assigns_key(pool)); conn end)` anonymous-function literal; `Process.put(:letflow_admission_refs, [ref | Process.get(:letflow_admission_refs, [])])`; and handle_errors/2's full body as a literal pipe/Enum.each/Process.delete sequence ending in a bare `conn`. These are complete, copy-paste-ready function bodies with real operators, pipes, and anonymous functions -- not @spec/@type signatures. This is the same class of violation that failed REQ-157's design gate twice; it is not acceptable here either.
checks_performed.acceptance_criteria_coverage: All 7 REQ-217 acceptance_criteria (read directly from docs/requirements.yaml, not paraphrased) map to a design section: AC1->§3/§7, AC2->§2/§3, AC3->§5 Mechanism A, AC4->§5 Mechanism B, AC5->§0/§3, AC6->§7, AC7 is a build/test-runner concern not a design concern. No TBD/deferral language found. Cross-module dependencies are listed in §0. This check passes on its own, but does not offset the two FAILs above.

issues: Rewrite §5's crash-safety analysis to correctly trace Plug.Router's dispatch/2 (deps/plug/lib/plug/router.ex:254-271) and Plug.Conn.WrapperError.reraise/4 (deps/plug/lib/plug/conn/wrapper_error.ex): a raise inside the matched ROUTE HANDLER is wrapped in WrapperError carrying the fully-downstream conn, which Plug.ErrorHandler's `rescue e in Plug.Conn.WrapperError` clause (not the `catch` clause) surfaces to handle_errors/2 -- so conn.assigns DOES carry both admission refs for that specific raise site. Re-justify the process-dictionary mechanism against the raise sites where it is actually needed: any raise inside a PLUG that runs before Plug.Router's dispatch/2 (TenantStatus, AuthPipeline, or Letflow.Plugs.Admission's own believed-unreachable tenant-derivation crash branches), which is NOT wrapped in WrapperError and does surface with the pre-pipeline conn via the `catch` clause. State this distinction explicitly in both the design doc and the eventual moduledoc -- do not claim a blanket 'nothing wraps in WrapperError in this codebase' fact that is false.

Correct OQ-1: lib/letflow/engine/wasm/host_api.ex and lib/letflow/engine/lua/platform.ex already establish a `@xxx_pdict_key` module-attribute naming convention for process-dictionary keys used to survive a callback/execution boundary. Follow that existing convention (e.g. a named module attribute, not a bare inline atom) instead of treating this as a novel, unprecedented idiom needing REVIEWER's blessing to invent a new pattern.

Remove all literal, runnable Elixir code from the design doc and replace with prose/@spec/@type only, per this project's own no-implementation-code rule (already enforced twice on REQ-157 for the identical violation class). Specifically: the pipe expression in §3; the assign/2 call, the register_before_send/2 anonymous-function literal, the two Process.put/Process.get/Process.delete lines, and handle_errors/2's full body in §5. Describe each as numbered prose steps (as §4.3/§8's own precedent in this repo already does for comparable cases), not as copy-paste-ready code.
result.verdict_statement: FAIL. Two independent hard-gate violations: (1) the design's single most safety-critical claim -- that nothing in this codebase's Plug/Bandit stack wraps a downstream raise in Plug.Conn.WrapperError, used to justify why conn.assigns is unreliable and a process-dictionary mechanism is required -- is factually wrong when independently verified against deps/plug/lib/plug/router.ex and deps/plug/lib/plug/conn/wrapper_error.ex, which the design's own §0 input list never even cites. The ultimate mechanism (process-dictionary release, Mechanism B) may still be necessary for other raise sites this design never distinguishes, but the stated justification is inaccurate and must be corrected before ELIXIR-DEV builds against it. (2) The design doc contains extensive literal, executable Elixir code (pipe expressions, an anonymous-function literal, Process.put/get/delete sequences, a full handle_errors/2 body) in violation of the no-implementation-code rule -- the identical violation class that already required two rework cycles on REQ-157 in this same repository. Routed back to CODE-DESIGNER with precise rework instructions; OQ-2 (tenant-derivation-failure crash-vs-Response.internal_error/1) is resolved by this review as acceptable as-is (crash, matching TenantStatus's fail-closed precedent) and does not need to be revisited.
